key_big: A thermometer measures how hot or cold something is.
body_html:
How to think about it

Our sense of touch can mislead us, so we measure temperature with a thermometer. A clinical thermometer (35 °C to 42 °C) measures body temperature, which is normally about 37 °C. A laboratory thermometer (−10 °C to 110 °C) measures the temperature of water and other substances.

Hold a thermometer by its end, not by the bulb. Keep a laboratory thermometer upright with the bulb in the liquid, not touching the container, and read it there. Digital thermometers are safer than mercury ones. The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin: K = °C + 273.15.

Example

Convert 27 °C into kelvin.

K = °C + 273.15

Answer: 300.15 K

Example

Which thermometer for boiling water?

needs to read 100 °C

Answer: a laboratory thermometer

Common mistakes

  • Using a clinical thermometer for hot water.
  • Taking a laboratory thermometer out of the water before reading it.
  • Holding the thermometer by its bulb.
